findings.text: Kept as an advisory under question 11. The reviewer cited line 505 of diff.patch; the file's own lines are 172-174. The new comment says geometric repacking is the default strategy from git 2.54 on, with no source. That disagrees with spec.md:27, where `gc.auto=1` alone repacked on git 2.54.0. The claim should name the version actually seen or be marked `[source?]`. Under the rubric, a defect is a rewrite that drops or alters a fact or invents a source. This is a new comment that alters no earlier text, so it stays advisory.

Lowered to an advisory as debt outside the change. This older test parses the `recordArgsTo` file inline here and again at line 570, the same parsing `recordedCalls` in tests/helpers/stub-git.ts already does. This diff did not write those lines.

Kept as an advisory under question 6. The reviewer cited line 509 of diff.patch; this is the file's line 177. The host now also passes `maintenance.geometric-repack.auto=1`, while AC-13 in spec.md:42 names only `gc.auto=1`. The test still fails when the runner's call is removed: with `maintenance.auto=false`, nothing else packs the objects in `objects/17`. So the criterion is proven, and only its wording lags the test.

Kept as an advisory, carried over from round 2. The reviewer cited line 492 of diff.patch; this is the file's line 160. Under a whole revert, AC-13's red is a race: the commit's own detached maintenance may pack the objects before the assertions run. With only the runner's call removed, the test fails every time, so a test does fail on reversion of the behaviour.
